summary:
Deliverables exist: analysis.py (runs end to end, cache in data/), results.json, figures/fig1-3 svg, notes.md, data_request.md.

Primary CPI test: YES. Weekly 1962–2026, n=3,383. In the worst 10% of S&P weeks (cutoff −2.40%), 10y Treasuries returned −0.17% a week when real-time CPI YoY was above 3% (194 tail weeks) and +0.33% otherwise (145). Gap −0.50 pp, stationary block-bootstrap 95% CI [−0.85, −0.20]. Block lengths 4–52 weeks, 5% and 20% tails, core CPI, an extra CPI lag, excluding carry, and defining the tail within each regime all give the same sign with CIs excluding zero. The regression interaction (HAC) is +0.142 (s.e. 0.031).

Breakeven tests (2003–2026): both NO. 10y tercile gap −0.34 pp, CI [−0.95, +0.38]. 5y5y gap +0.46 pp (wrong sign), CI [−0.20, +1.20]. Only 35–49 tail weeks per tercile, so these are inconclusive rather than contradicting.

Main caveat (exploratory, added after the primary result): era and inflation regime are confounded. Within 1962–1999 the gap is −0.28 pp, CI [−0.64, +0.13]. Within 2000–2026 it is −0.25 pp, CI [−0.77, +0.37]. The pooled gap is larger because high-CPI weeks are mostly 1966–1999 and low-CPI tail weeks are mostly 2000–2020. A difference-in-differences version still excludes zero in the full sample and in 1962–1999.

Sub-periods: the 1970s have 65 tail weeks, all high-CPI, with mean −0.30% (CI [−0.59, −0.06]). 2022 has 16 tail weeks with mean −0.69%. 2000–2020 has mean +0.74%.

Proxy validation against IEF after 2002: correlation 0.98. Pre-2002 accuracy is unvalidated. CPI release timing is approximated (15th of the following month, not ALFRED vintages). The fig3 title was rewritten to match verified return-correlation signs. notes.md lists 8 limits and next steps.
